run_history.interpretation: Previous 240-second stop was a harness budget limit, not a suite failure. Completed at 319 seconds under timeout 600; the clean-approval assertion reported a genuine post-approval change from an in-flight editor save (harness timing on slow hardware). Passes on faster hardware. Not a React defect certification.

results.diagnosis: Harness timing weakness on slower hardware, not a build defect or port gap. The suite runs two concurrent-edit steps (two editors in the same field, then a Load-their-version click) with only 800-900 ms of settle time before the reviewer approves. On this hardware an editor save was still in flight when writeSignoff hashed the content, so it landed after approval and the material genuinely changed. The observed ["Changed after approval","Changed after approval","Changed after approval"] is the safeguard working correctly — the very next assertion ("words changed after approval: everyone is told, the viewer included") expects exactly those three values and passed. An earlier guess that the deferred project-summary write raced the sign-off hash was wrong: the summary write targets the project document, not the material, and sameApproval already tries seven canonical forms. Verified passing on the supplier's faster hardware, where the assertion returns ["","",""].
results.safeguard_preserved: signCanon, sameApproval, signedAsStored and writeSignoff left untouched; changing them to turn the suite green would break a genuine safeguard the following assertion depends on.
results.deterministic_rerun_note: To make the suite deterministic, wait for quiescence before the approval step — poll until no page has a pending save — instead of relying on fixed timeouts.
results.interpretation: Completed in 317 seconds with timeout 600. The clean-approval assertion reported a real post-approval change caused by an in-flight editor save from the preceding concurrent-edit steps; the change-detection mechanism behaved correctly. Classified timing-sensitive on slow hardware, passes on faster hardware; not a React defect certification.
